data.title: APAC Realty to buy remaining 9.4% stake of ERA Indonesia for $1.6m
data.description:
It is offering $0.02 (IDR250) per unit for the remaining 89.3 million shares.

APAC Realty plans to acquire the remaining 9.4% stake in PT ERA Graharealty Tbk (ERA Indonesia) for about $1.6m in connection with the proposed delisting of the unit from the Indonesia Stock Exchange.

It is offering $0.02 (IDR250) per share for the remaining 89.3 million shares through a voluntary tender offer. The acquisition will be funded using internal resources.

The Singapore-listed property services group currently owns about 90.6% of ERA Indonesia, or 860.6 million shares.

The acquisition and delisting are expected to be completed by March 2027, subject to the required approvals.

APAC Realty said the proposed acquisition and delisting are intended to give management greater flexibility, reduce listing compliance costs, and improve operational efficiency.

“ERA Indonesia no longer requires funding from the capital markets and has no plans to raise funds from the capital markets in the future,” it added.

The transaction is not expected to have a material impact on the group’s net tangible assets per share or earnings per share for the financial year ending 31 December 2026.

The deal remains subject to approvals from ERA Indonesia’s independent shareholders and Indonesian regulators.

data.title: Aesen hybrid crew boat targets 40% fuel savings
data.description:
Energy storage helps optimise engine loading across offshore missions.

Singapore-based Aesen has introduced the Aesen 116H, a next-generation hybrid crew boat designed for offshore personnel transportation and infield logistics, the company said in a statement on 11 September.

The vessel combines hybrid propulsion technology and energy storage systems, with an estimated 30% to 40% reduction in fuel consumption compared with conventionally powered crew boats operating under similar duty cycles.

Aesen 116H is designed to optimise engine loading and power utilisation during short transits, variable power demands and standby periods.

The vessel incorporates a multi-layered redundancy philosophy to improve operational continuity and reliability across a range of operational contingencies.

It also features Smart Window technology, which enhances situational awareness on the bridge by improving visibility of critical operating areas around the vessel.

The technology complements conventional navigation and monitoring systems to support decision-making in complex offshore operating conditions, Aesen said.

data.title: Fraud risks drive tighter identity checks in digital services
data.description:
Singapore recorded a 17.59% fraud signal rate, according to a report by Shufti Sphere.

Singapore’s expanding digital services are putting greater focus on identity verification as businesses face fraud risks and tighter regulatory scrutiny, according to a report by Shufti Sphere.

Singpass facilitates more than 41 million digital transactions each month. Across Asia-Pacific, identity verification is used for account openings, KYC checks, payment authentication, lending decisions, and marketplace seller onboarding.

Singapore recorded a 17.59% fraud signal rate in Shufti’s internal identity verification data sample. The company said fraud rates varied across the region, with some of the highest rates per 1,000 verifications recorded in digitally mature economies.

The risks are also drawing greater regulatory attention in Singapore. The Monetary Authority of Singapore’s September 2025 information paper on cyber risks associated with deepfakes raised supervisory expectations around AI-generated identity fraud, synthetic media, and remote onboarding.

The paper highlighted the need to protect non-face-to-face verification processes against manipulated video, impersonation, and deepfake-enabled attacks.

Across APAC, businesses are also dealing with deepfake injection, synthetic identities, and forged documents as digital commerce, payments and public digital infrastructure expand. The region contributes nearly 60% of global economic growth, whilst social commerce and real-time payments continue to scale.

Shufti said identity verification providers face challenges in supporting the region’s wide range of identity documents and writing systems. Many OCR systems are built around Latin alphabets and Western identity documents, creating difficulties when processing scripts including Chinese, Korean, Thai, Khmer, Bengali, and Devanagari.

The company also said some verification providers rely on third-party technology for OCR, face matching and deepfake detection, which can make it harder to adapt systems to new fraud methods and regulatory requirements.

Poor verification can also affect customer acquisition and retention through onboarding friction, whilst successful fraud can result in losses linked to mule accounts, synthetic identities, fraudulent loans, and scams.

Singapore’s $3b-plus money-laundering case further highlighted the financial consequences of weak controls.

The case involved more than $3b in seized or frozen assets and led to $27.45m in combined composition penalties against nine financial institutions in 2025.

data.title: AI investment slowdown could weigh on economic growth, Gan says
data.description:
A sharp fall in AI-related spending could trigger corrections in global financial markets.

Singapore’s economy could face weaker growth if global investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure slows sharply, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) Gan Kim Yong said.

AI-related activity is expected to contribute significantly to Singapore’s economic growth in both the near and longer term. Strong global investment in AI infrastructure has benefited outward-oriented sectors linked to related supply chains, including electronics, precision engineering, and machinery, equipment, and supplies wholesale trade.

“Downside risks to global AI capital expenditure include tighter financial conditions globally, which could make financing more costly for these investments,” Gan said.

A sudden drop in AI-related spending could also weaken investor confidence and trigger sharp corrections in global financial markets, with spillover effects on global economic activity, he added.

However, Singapore’s economy is diversified, with information and communications, professional services, real estate, and construction also expected to support GDP growth for the rest of 2026.

The government is also supporting businesses at different stages of AI readiness to adopt the technology and undertake AI-driven transformation to improve productivity and innovation. It is helping workers build the skills needed to work with AI, take on redesigned roles, and move into higher-value opportunities.

Around three in 10 firms have adopted AI, according to a recent Ministry of Manpower survey. Of these firms, about seven in 10 reported improvements in worker productivity. Gan said AI is complementing rather than replacing labour, with more firms redesigning existing roles and creating new AI-related jobs instead of reducing headcount.

A recent Ministry of Trade and Industry study also found that firms using AI recorded higher revenue and total employment, whilst those that deepened their AI capabilities saw greater gains.

Singapore is also building its AI research, engineering and commercialisation capabilities through National AI Missions in advanced manufacturing, financial services, connectivity, and healthcare announced at Budget 2026.

"The Government will continue to monitor the impact of AI on our economy, including enterprise-level AI adoption and its effects on firm performance," said Gan. "Through the National AI Council, we will coordinate our national AI efforts and ensure that AI-driven growth benefits the wider economy."

data.title: Three in four S-REITs readying for sustainability assurance ahead of 2029 mandate: PwC
data.description:
About 75% use either ESG-specific or generic systems for data collection and reporting.

Three in four Singapore REITs (S-REITs) have conducted or are preparing for a sustainability assurance readiness assessment ahead of mandatory external limited assurance for Scope 1 and 2 emissions from FY2029.

About 75% of surveyed S-REITs use either ESG-specific or generic systems for sustainability data collection and reporting, according to a PwC Singapore report.

Half use dedicated ESG systems, whilst another quarter use generic systems.

Under Singapore’s climate reporting requirements, all listed companies are required to report Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions from FY2025.

PwC said 90% of S-REITs are able to complete their sustainability data collection and reporting within four months of their financial year-end.

However, only 15% have obtained external assurance over sustainability-related information, whilst another 25% plan to do so.

Data collection also remains a challenge, particularly where information on energy, water and waste is held by tenants, property managers and other service providers, the report added.

The study covered 20 S-REITs representing 48% of the sector’s $201b in assets under management as of March 2026.

Separately, the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority in July opened a consultation on draft Singapore Sustainability Disclosure Standards, which runs until 25 October.

The authority also launched a Sustainability Assurance Body of Knowledge to support training for professionals involved in verifying climate disclosures.

Sustainability-linked financing has meanwhile remained active amongst listed REITs.

Elite UK REIT recently secured an $86.5m sustainability-linked Shariah-compliant facility from Maybank and RHB, which will partly finance property acquisitions, refinance existing loans, and support working capital.

The financing also allows for adjustments to margins if the REIT improves the energy performance certificate ratings of its properties.

data.title: Businesses restructure amidst sector growth
data.description:
New registrations exceeded cessations in manufacturing and retail.

Businesses continue to restructure and relocate parts of their operations in response to cost, technology, and supply chain considerations amidst growth in Singapore's manufacturing and retail trade sectors.

Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) Dr Tan See Leng said in an oral answer to Parliament on 9 September that manufacturing grew 7.3% year on year (YoY) in the first quarter (Q1) and 12.5% in the second quarter (Q2).

Retail trade also grew 2.5% YoY in Q1 and 1.0% in Q2.

“In both sectors, the number of new business registrations exceeded the number of business cessations over the first half of the year,” Tan said.

He said businesses regularly review and optimise their operations in response to changing market conditions.

“A company may shift its production to regional countries for cost optimisation, whilst retaining its headquarters here to benefit from Singapore's ecosystem, for functions such as product development, regulatory and quality oversight, distribution, and supply chain planning,” he added.

Singapore's economy expanded 6.1% in the first half of the year, following full-year growth of 5.3% in 2024 and 5.0% in 2025.

Tan said Singapore's value proposition to businesses remains strong, citing the Economic Development Board's (EDB) $8.9b in total business expenditure commitments in 2025.

The majority of the commitments came from investments in headquarters, professional services, and research and development.

The EDB also secured $14.2b in fixed asset investment commitments, including about $12.1b from manufacturing-related projects.

“The Government closely monitors the economic conditions to ensure that we remain an attractive hub for businesses and sustain the supply of good jobs for our people,” Tan said.

He said the government will continue to support businesses and workers to pivot, grow, and pursue opportunities in advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, high-value trust-based services, quantum, and space, in line with the Economic Strategy Review recommendations.

data.title: Metrocon raises $4.6m from 23-million-share placement
data.description:
The proceeds will fund growth initiatives.

Metrocon Holdings Limited, formerly known as Hatten Land, raised gross proceeds of $4.6m from a compliance placement of 23 million new ordinary shares at $0.20 each.

The company said the proceeds will mainly fund growth initiatives, including upgrading its Building and Construction Authority registration to Grade L6 under the CR08 piling works workhead.

It added that the funds will be used to strengthen its workforce and pursue business expansion opportunities.

Trading in Metrocon’s shares under its new name is expected to begin on 15 September.

The placement increased the company’s issued and paid-up share capital to about 176.9 million shares from 153.9 million shares.

Metrocon’s public float stood at about 26.2% of its enlarged share capital, comprising 12.6% held by scheme creditors, 13% by investors under the compliance placement, and 0.6% held by other public shareholders.

data.title: SGX daily securities trading value jumps 35% to $2.2b in August
data.description:
Total securities market turnover rose 29% to $43.3b.

The securities daily average value (SDAV) on the Singapore Exchange climbed 35% year on year (YoY) to $2.2b in August on the back of strong interest from institutional and retail investors.

The SDAV was also 8% higher month on month (MoM). Total securities market turnover rose 29% YoY to $43.3b.

Retail activity rose 11% MoM in small- and mid-cap stocks and 22% in real estate investment trusts, with investors buying during market pullbacks, the SGX Group said.

On a yearly basis, trading in Straits Times Index (STI) constituents climbed 44% to $1.5b. The benchmark extended its rally and reached a month-end high of 5,755.36.

STI exchange-traded funds recorded an 18th consecutive month of net inflows, totalling $1.6b and lifting assets under management to $5.8b.

Daily average volume for SGX Straits Times Index Futures more than doubled month on month, whilst open interest reached a record $49.5m in notional value on 28 August.

Open interest in SGX MSCI Singapore Index Futures rose to $11.8b in notional value at month-end, whilst daily average volume reached an all-time high of $2.98b.

Foreign-exchange derivatives posted strong growth as US dollar weakness increased portfolio hedging. Total listed FX derivatives volume jumped 47% YoY to 8.1 million contracts.

Overall derivatives traded volume, however, slipped 1% to 27.1 million contracts, with daily average volume down 2% to 1.3 million contracts.

Secondary fundraising on the bourse reached $3.57b in the first eight months.
